title: Save and open
learned: Ctrl+S (or Ctrl+Shift+S, Save as) saves the patch: modules, cables, every knob and the Editor song
File > Open (Ctrl+O) and File > Open recent bring a patch back
Save often; Ctrl+Z only remembers this session

steps.why: A patch can take a while to build. Saving it keeps everything exactly as it is.
steps.do: This is the patch from the first-sound lesson, with one change: the oscillator plays from its MIX output, so the MORPH knob changes the wave shape. Press Next.
Turn FREQ or MORPH of the oscillator to a sound you like.
steps.after: Next to the patch name in the top bar you now see * edited: the patch has changes that are not saved.

steps.why: A saved patch is one .vcv file.
steps.do: Press Ctrl+Shift+S (File > Save as / Export), pick a folder and a name, and save. In the standalone app, Ctrl+S does the same for a patch that has no file yet; in a DAW, Ctrl+S only saves a patch that already has a file, so use Ctrl+Shift+S the first time.
steps.after: The file holds every module, cable and knob position, and the song of the Editor if there is one. Copy it to another computer and it opens the same. In a DAW the patch is also kept inside the DAW project, but a file lets you open it anywhere: in another project or in the standalone app.

steps.why: Opening a patch replaces the one in the rack, so this lesson only shows you where.
steps.do: Open the File menu in the top bar and look: Open (Ctrl+O), Open recent, Save as / Export (Ctrl+Shift+S). Press Next.
steps.after: Open recent is the quickest way back to what you worked on last.

steps.do: You finished the basics. The next categories build real instruments, rhythms and songs. Press Next.
